title: Rollout runway and stoplight framework (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a lightweight, cross‑functional rollout framework focused on predictable canaries and A/B experiments. The goal is a repeatable "stoplight" gating flow teams can run with minimal ops involvement while preserving safety and quick rollback capability. Use this doc to align product, infra, serving, SRE, and CS on responsibilities, signals, and actions during progressive rollouts.

Why this is different:
- Emphasizes a simple stoplight (green/yellow/red) operator model that can be surfaced in the Console UI and used to trigger automated rollback/fallback rules.
- Explicit allocation of runway phases (lab -> dark launch -> canary -> ramp -> full) with decision checkpoints and timeboxes.
- Adds a compact failure-mode & blast-radius quantification table to inform slice sizing and guardrail thresholds.
- Designed to be machine-checkable where possible: health checks, error rate thresholds, latency p50/p95 SLOs, and regression windows are formalized.

Runway phases (names + intent + owners):
1) Local / Lab (owner: feature team)
   - intent: validate shape and basic correctness against unit/integration tests and a small internal dataset.
   - boundary: no traffic, no customer exposure.
   - artifact: gated smoke tests, model eval report, performance benchmark.

2) Dark launch (owner: feature team + infra)
   - intent: run feature in prod path without routing decisions (observability-only).
   - boundary: 0% traffic; shadow requests allowed for end-to-end validation.
   - guardrails: latency budget check, error surface reconciliation, storage/access permissions.

3) Canary (owner: product + oncall SRE)
   - intent: run on a small user slice to validate product metrics and infra stability.
   - typical slices: 1% global traffic OR 5% internal beta org traffic depending on blast radius.
   - duration: timebox 24–72 hours by default; extend only on green.

4) Ramp (owner: product + SRE + solutions engineering)
   - intent: progressive traffic increase with automated checks at each step (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50%).
   - duration: per-step timebox (12–48 hours) with human signoff required to pass out of any step that flips to yellow.

5) Full / GA (owner: product + infra)
   - intent: feature considered fully released with long‑term monitoring retained.
   - actions: tag release, start scheduled quality regression checks, integrate into Optimize recommendations.

Stoplight gating model (definitions + actions):
- GREEN: all critical signals within thresholds. Continue to next runway phase or maintain traffic. No intervention. Log pass event and continue.
- YELLOW: one or more non-critical regressions (soft signals). Take caution: increase sampling, enable additional tracing, optionally pause ramp, notify owners and schedule 1-hour troubleshooting window. If yellow persists beyond timebox, escalate to Red.
- RED: critical regression (high error spike, p95 latency > threshold, data leak). Automated rollback to previous compatible model/variant and open incident. Trigger postmortem prerequisites.

Signals and suggested thresholds (machine-checkable where possible):
- Error rate (5xx or model-health exceptions): green < 0.2% of requests; yellow 0.2–1%; red > 1% sustained for 5m.
- Latency (inference p95): green within baseline + 30%; yellow baseline + 30–80%; red > baseline + 80% or p99 regression. Baseline defined in model performance profile.
- Cost/throughput: unexpected token-level cost per minute increase > 2x baseline -> yellow; sustained >3x -> red.
- Quality signals (product metric regressions): precise thresholds are product dependent (e.g., conversion drop > 5% absolute or 10% relative -> yellow; >10% absolute -> red).
- Safety/Content violations: any elevated safety signal that reaches escalation rules -> immediate red.

Failure-mode & blast-radius guide (use to pick initial slice sizes):
- Mode: correctness/regression in output (blast radius = user-visible content). Start with small customer subset or internal-only slice.
- Mode: resource-exhaustion (GPU OOM, KV cache thrash). Blast radius = region or cluster; start with local region-only canary.
- Mode: data exfil/permission bug. Blast radius = tenant-level; default to internal-only beta.

Roles & responsibilities (practical checklist):
- Feature team (owner): provide rollout plan, expected metrics, smoke tests, evaluation artifact, and rollback variant. Keep a single person on pager during canary and ramp.
- SRE / Infra: configure traffic slices, autoscaling policies, resource quotas, and monitor infra signals; own automated rollback triggers tied to stoplight red.
- Product: define product KPI deltas, pick user segments for experiments, and own A/B statistical significance plan.
- Observability/RE: ensure dashboards exist for new metrics, instrument trace links, and set data retention for experiment windows.
- CS / Support: prepare canned KB updates (if behavior may change for users), set filters for incoming tickets to allow rapid triage.

A/B experiment hygiene (quick checklist):
- Hypothesis in 1 sentence and primary metric defined.
- Minimum detectable effect and required sample size computed.
- Randomization method documented (cookie vs. user-id vs. account).
- Data pipelines tagged with experiment id to avoid contamination.
- Safety fallback: route traffic to control model if experiment toggles to red.

Automated gating examples (implementation notes):
- Implement stoplight as a small state machine in the Console. Each runway step registers a guard condition set (thresholds + window). If a condition violates for n consecutive evaluation windows, state flips to YELLOW/RED and actions trigger.
- Use temporal windows: evaluate 5m/15m/60m windows depending on metric sensitivity.
- Persist stoplight state and reason (for audit). Link to incident and PR/rollout that triggered it.

Operational playbook (short):
- Pre-canary checklist (to run 24–48h before): smoke tests pass, dashboards provisioned, rollback artifact verified, paging rotations set, communication channel (Slack #rollout-XYZ) created.
- Canary day: start time, slice id, owner oncall, expected baseline numbers posted, monitoring links shared. Do not change unrelated infra during first 12h.
- If YELLOW: open joint triage meeting within 60 minutes. Increase sampling and collect traces. Decide to continue/pause/rollback.
- If RED: automated rollback executed. Incident recorded. Engineers run postmortem within 5 working days.

Data & analysis artifacts to produce during the run: list of traces, sample requests (anonymized), metric timeseries with annotated window boundaries, failure logs, cost burn rate table, and a short verdict note (green/yellow/red + reason).

Unresolved questions / open decisions (ACTION items):
- Default slice sizing heuristic: should we prefer percent-of-global-users or percent-of-orgs for initial canary? (owner: product)
- Exact p95 latency thresholds: do we standardize a multiplier (e.g., baseline * 1.3) or use absolute ms bands per model class? (owner: serving runtime)
- How to coordinate cross‑region rollouts when private deployments exist with different capacity limits? (owner: private-deployments)
- Who is authorized to override automated red rollbacks for business-critical experiments and what audit is required? (owner: legal/compliance + product)

Short-term next steps (two-week sprint plan):
- Finalize the stoplight UI mock in Console (owner: console-and-tooling). Due: 2025-01-20.
- Wire a simple state machine that takes metric inputs and emits stoplight status (owner: observability). Prototype: 2025-02-05.
- Pilot this flow on a low-risk internal feature (owner: product). Pilot window: 2025-02-10 to 2025-02-18.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight. The aim is fast adoption — teams should be able to run this without a heavy ops ceremony.
- Please leave comments inline in this doc with specific threshold suggestions or edge cases from your team’s past incidents.

Quick reference (TL;DR):
- Use the five runway phases.
- Stoplight (Green/Yellow/Red) drives automation and human actions.
- Guardrail thresholds should be machine-enforceable where possible.
- Small safe canaries + clear rollback artifacts = lower blast radius.

Appendix: example stoplight reasons (short list):
- "inference-5xx-spike": sudden server error spike
- "p95-latency-regression": >80% over baseline for 15m
- "conversion-drop": primary product KPI down >10% vs control
- "safety-alert-elevated": content filter hit rate above safety alert threshold

-- end working draft --

TODOs (please pick and assign in next sync):
- [ ] Product: pick 2 pilot features and owner names.
- [ ] Observability: draft metric templates for stoplight evaluation.
- [ ] SRE: prepare automated rollback playbook and permission model.
- [ ] Console: design signal badges and stateful stoplight UI.
summary: Working draft of a compact stoplight-based progressive rollout framework with runway phases, machine-checkable guardrails, role checklists, and operational playbook. Meant to be piloted and iterated.
